## plugin:context7:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

lastPrompt: You orchestrator. Delegate to subagents!  Resolve issues #223 to #238. Ask your questions first, so that you can further work in autonomy

content.text: I'll pull the issues first, then come back with questions.

input.command:
for n in $(seq 223 238); do echo "=== #$n ==="; gh issue view $n --json number,title,state,labels,body 2>/dev/null | jq -r '"\(.state) | \(.title)
labels: \(.labels|map(.name)|join(", "))
---

The snippet-question leaves the instructions for the "snippet editor" in the scrollback. Unnecessary. ``` ? What is /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor on pc1? One application — /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor is what would be reproduced on pc2 ? How should pc2 get /opt/pcsw-uat-app? ◆ /opt/pcsw-uat-app install These commands run on pc2 with nobody watching — there is no keyboard attached to them, so a command that asks a question (e.g. a debconf prompt) hangs the sync instead of failing. Log only shows the "apt-get" commands (in DEBUG, as required), but nothing in FULL log. FULL log must list every item action install/remove/update/... of every package-sync job. If that is not in docs/planning/package-sync-user-requirements.md yet, add it and apply it to everything that flows from there, a.o. docs/planning/package-sync-conformance-criteria.md, docs/dev/package-sync-scenario-coverage.md, tests, code, docs.

content.subject: #226 Drop "report" prefix from version-difference lines
content.description: Render as `tree: pc1 has X, pc2 has Y` — no leading word, no duplicated source version.

content.subject: #227 Per-case title and explanation-first for collateral question
content.description: Name the machine explicitly ("marked as pc2's own"), lift the concrete explanation above the key legend, and make the title case-specific if the question is raised per item.

content.subject: #228 Retitle repository-deletion question
content.description: "Delete apt repositories pc1 no longer has" instead of "Delete repositories pc1 no longer has (apt)".

content.subject: #229 Clearer snap version question
content.description: Title "Align snap package versions", key label "align", detail names the source of the revision.

content.description: Title asks "How should pc2 get X?" but the options are install/skip/never — retitle to the install decision.

content.subject: #231 --allow-first-sync is ignored
content.description: Flag set on the command line yet the first-sync overwrite confirmation still appears. Trace CLI -> context -> confirmation check and fix.

content.subject: #233 Narrow the snapd auto-refresh hold to snap_sync
content.description: Hold is taken before apt_sync runs, far wider than needed. Scope it to the snap sync window.

content.subject: #234 snapd pause logged twice
content.description: Determine whether the two DEBUG lines are source+target (correct) or a genuine double-pause, and fix or clarify accordingly.

content.subject: #235 flatpak_sync shows no progress line while applying
content.description: Status line sits in flatpak_sync with no progress line while changes apply. Report progress the way apt_sync/snap_sync do.

content.subject: #236 Snippet editor instructions should not stay in scrollback
content.description: Other questions collapse to title+answer after answering; the multiline snippet prompt leaves its instruction block behind.

content.description: Registry stores the body with trailing whitespace, forcing an ugly YAML block. Strip at capture, before anything is done with it.

content.description: Per-item install/remove/upgrade actions appear only in the DEBUG command trace. Add the requirement to package-sync-user-requirements.md and cascade it: conformance criteria, scenario coverage, tests, code, docs.

Two findings you should know about:

**#225 landed on the fallback, not live rendering.** It was tested under a real pty rather than reasoned about: with Live auto-refreshing, `Prompt.ask` writes onto the live region's last row and the next 10 Hz tick erases it — the question survived ~100 ms. Rich's `LiveRender` anchors at the cursor and rewrites upward, clobbering any output it didn't route itself; prompt_toolkit screens are worse. Fixing it properly means owning the input loop. So the last frame now stays in scrollback above the question, which is what your issue named as the acceptable fallback.

**#231 was narrower than the issue suggested.** `--allow-out-of-order` was never broken — `_check_out_of_order` already short-circuits before reaching the confirmer. Only `--allow-first-sync` reached the prompt. The confirmer fix covers both paths regardless.

#237 required amending `PKG-FR-SNIPPET-VERBATIM`, which said snippets are stored "exactly as written" — directly contradicted by stripping. That's now worded to permit the capture-time strip.

All 15 pushed; CI is running on PR #206. One correction to what I told you earlier about #238, and one thing to decide.

**#238's premise was wrong, and it matters.** Nothing was suppressing the `sl` line — it *was* in the FULL log, and apt is not batched (`packages.install` issues one `apt-get` per diff). The line read `install sl (6.03-1)`: no manager, no machine, and visually indistinguishable from the thousands of DEBUG `apt-get install …` traces surrounding it, which is why a grep found only the commands. It also had zero test coverage. The fix is therefore about identifiability, not about a missing write: the line is now `apt: install sl (6.03-1) on nomad`, emitted from `PackageSyncJob._converge_one` so all four managers share it. The requirement, `PKG-FR-LOG-ACTIONS`, conformance traceability (135→136 articles) and matrix rows J172/J173 all landed as you asked.

**#235's cause was the shared framework, not flatpak.** Progress was reported only *after* each item completed, and the UI creates a job's bar on the first update — so any single-item job showed no bar at all, for its entire duration. Reporting now happens before each item and carries the item name; flatpak additionally reports its pre-loop remote provisioning, which is the silent window your screenshot caught.

One housekeeping note: the two final agents shared the working tree, and `b04edaef` swept the J172/J173 matrix rows into its commit rather than `971ec936`. The content is all on the branch — only the attribution is off. Say the word if you want that untangled; I'd leave it.

Once CI is green I'll take the lock and drive a real `pc-switcher sync` on pc1 to eyeball the TUI changes — #223 wrapping, #225 context-during-prompt, #227's new screen layout, #236's collapse and #235's progress bar are all things only a real terminal can confirm. === PR body ===
Replicates installed packages from source to target across apt, snap and flatpak, plus the repository/keyring/remote state those installs depend on, with every difference surfaced for an explicit decision before any change is applied.

## What this delivers

- Three jobs — `apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync` — over a shared package-sync core (declarative manifest capture, item-level convergence via each ecosystem's own tooling; package databases are never rsynced, see ADR-020).
- A `PackagePhaseCoordinator` that runs every enabled manager's `plan()`, renders **one** batched review across all managers, then runs `apply()`. No manager can mutate the target before the others have diffed.
- Removals presented in their own group with a concrete removal verb, never sharing a group with installs, so a bulk tick cannot silently delete.
- The full diff-class taxonomy: missing-on-target, extra-on-target, version-mismatch, held/pinned, repo-unavailable, unreproducible. Versions float; a mismatch is reported with both versions and never force-downgraded.
- `/etc/apt` repository state as items — sources, per-repo keyrings, legacy trust keys, pins, apt config — converged in apt's required order, transactionally, with rollback if `apt-get update` fails.
- Machine-local decision files (skip-always), inert in both source and target roles, never synced.
- A shared, synced install-snippet registry for items no package manager can reproduce.
- Enabling a package job automatically excludes that ecosystem's store from `folder_sync`; package jobs run before `folder_sync` so apps are provisioned before their data lands.

## Process

Planned, then peer-reviewed by Codex (gpt-5.5) against the repo. That review found nine defects, all independently re-verified and fixed by replanning before any code was written — including that the original design would have let `apt_sync` mutate the target before the other managers had diffed, and that `send_file` (plain SFTP as the SSH user) could never have written into `/etc/apt`.

A deep code review after implementation found two further blockers, both fixed with regression tests: a `KeyError` crash path that violated continue-on-item-failure, and `install` without `-D` failing on targets where `/etc/apt/keyrings` does not exist.

All 15 issues are resolved, verified, and labelled `status:done`. Lock released, VMs back at baseline.

**Verification is complete on all three levels you asked for.** Local gate green (ruff, format, codespell, basedpyright, 4468 unit tests). PR #206 green on all nine checks including the 38-minute VM integration suite. Three things to note:

**Two issues did not need the fix they asked for**, and I did not force one. #234 was never a double-pause — one call site looping source and target — so only the log's legibility changed. #233's narrowing would have reopened a real race, since `folder_sync` mirrors `~/snap/<app>/<rev>` by the revision `snap_sync` just converged; you chose to keep the wide window and fix the reporting, and the log line now states exactly that reasoning on the machine it applies to.

**#238's premise turned out to be wrong** — the line was already being written at FULL level and apt was never batched. What was actually missing was identifiability and any test coverage at all. Worth knowing, because the requirement I added (`PKG-FR-LOG-ACTIONS`) is now what stops it regressing.

**One new finding, outside the scope you gave me, so I left it alone**: `snap_sync.py:829,831` writes FULL log lines as `source snap refresh.hold: (none)` / `target snap refresh.hold: (none)`, using role words where the runbook's own rule requires hostnames. Say the word and I'll file it or fix it.

async def _hold_snap_autorefresh(self) -> None:
        """Pause snapd AUTOMATIC refreshes on both hosts for the sync window (decision 4).

        Gated on `sync_jobs.snap_sync` being enabled and skipped in dry-run (writing
        `refresh.hold` is a system mutation; ADR-014/D-12). Captures each host's prior
        `refresh.hold` first so `_cleanup` can restore it exactly, marks the hold engaged,
        then applies a timed hold on each host WHOSE PRIOR POLICY IT COULD READ. Only touches
        the system-wide `refresh.hold` option — never per-snap holds — and never blocks the
        manual `--revision` convergence snap_sync performs.

        A host whose capture failed is left untouched (`PKG-FR-SNAP-REFRESH-PAUSE`). The
        capture is what makes the write reversible: without a pre-sync value there is nothing
        to put back, so setting the option would replace an unknown policy — possibly the
        user's own indefinite hold — with a timed one that expires into "no hold at all". The
        cost is running unpaused on that host, which risks a mid-run auto-refresh; that trade
        is the criterion's, and it is the same one `_restore_snap_hold` makes on the way out.
        """
        if self._dry_run or not self._config.sync_jobs.get("snap_sync", False):
            return

        self._snap_hold_prior_source, self._snap_hold_readable_source = await self._capture_snap_hold(Host.SOURCE)
        self._snap_hold_prior_target, self._snap_hold_readable_target = await self._capture_snap_hold(Host.TARGET)
        # Engage BEFORE applying so a partially-applied hold is still restored in _cleanup.
        self._snap_hold_engaged = True
        for host, prior, readable in (
            (Host.SOURCE, self._snap_hold_prior_source, self._snap_hold_readable_source),
            (Host.TARGET, self._snap_hold_prior_target, self._snap_hold_readable_target),
        ):
            if not readable:
                self._logger.warning(
                    "Not pausing snapd auto-refresh on %s: its refresh.hold could not be read, so a hold "
                    "written here could not be put back. The sync continues unpaused on that machine.",
                    self._machine_name(host),
                    extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": host.value},
                )
                continue
            # One line per machine, naming it (#234). The pause is two separate writes of
            # the SAME command text, one per host, so the DEBUG trace shows the identical
            # `snap set system refresh.hold` twice; a single "on both hosts" summary left a
            # reader grepping the log unable to tell that pair from one pause applied twice.
            # The line also states its owner and its span (#233): the pause happens before
            # the first job, which read as an unexplained stop with no component behind it.
            self._logger.info(
                "Pausing snapd auto-refresh on %s for the whole run — held by the orchestrator, not by "
                "snap_sync alone, because snap_sync converges each snap's revision and folder_sync then "
                "mirrors that revision's data directory; a refresh between the two drops it from the mirror",
                self._machine_name(host),
                extra={"job": "orchestrator", "host": host.value},
            )

# Python Development Conventions

Apply to Python code/projects. New or owner-controlled projects: use defaults. Existing: follow project config (Python version, deps, tests, lint, CI) unless explicitly migrating. Use modern standards for supported version.

## Python Version and Modern Practices

- New Python projects: target >=3.14
- Existing projects: use modern syntax for configured version
- Use modern type syntax: e.g. `str | None` instead of `Optional[str]`, `list[str]` instead of `List[str]`
- Include `from __future__ import annotations` when improves annotation behavior for Python version
- Use `@override` for method overrides when available in Python version
- Prefer `StrEnum` for string-based enums when available in Python version
- Prefer `Path` from pathlib for local filesystem paths

## Project Setup and Developer Workflows

- MUST use uv for running code, managing dependencies in new projects
- Existing projects: use project's workflow. Don't replace Poetry/Hatch/tox/Makefiles unless asked
- Use plain uv commands: `uv sync`, `uv run ...`, `uv add`, etc. Avoid `uv pip`. NEVER use `uv pip install` unless project intentionally uses uv's pip-compatible interface
- Use `codespell` for checking typos in code/comments
- Use `ruff` for linting, formatting
- Use `basedpyright` for type checking
- Use `pytest` for testing

## Code Quality Standards

- Full type annotations for function signatures, modern syntax per Python version
- Import types from correct modules (e.g., use `collections.abc` not `typing` for collection types)
- Proper error handling with specific exception types, meaningful messages
- Single responsibility principle, keep functions focused
- Use context managers for resource management
- Prefer composition over inheritance
- Self-documenting code with meaningful names
- Follow PEP 8 (max 119 chars), use Python strengths, avoid anti-patterns

## Documentation Philosophy

- Document architectural decisions, design patterns
- Concise docstrings: focus on "why" not obvious "what"
- Explain complex logic rationales inline when needed
- Use backticks for variable/parameter names in docstrings
- Avoid repetitive or obvious comments

## Testing Strategy

- Small focused tests, clear locality. Use repo's layout (colocated, `tests/` tree, doctests)
- Avoid trivial tests that test language itself
- Simple assertions over complex pytest fixtures when possible
- Test edge cases, errors, boundary values
- Mock external dependencies, I/O operations appropriately
- Mocked integration behavior: add real-dep integration coverage where practical
- Never use `assert False` - raise `AssertionError` with explanation instead

## Performance Optimization Techniques

- Use appropriate data structures (sets for membership, deque for queues, etc.)
- Implement generators for memory-efficient iteration over large datasets
- Apply caching strategies where beneficial
- Utilize built-in functions/libraries (itertools, collections, functools)
- Consider algorithmic complexity, choose efficient algorithms
- Profile code using cProfile, line_profiler, or memory_profiler before optimizing

## Error Handling and Type Checking

- Use `# pyright: ignore` sparingly, always with explanation
- Raise `AssertionError` with descriptive messages for invariant violations
- Handle exceptions at appropriate levels, avoid bare except
- Use specific exception types that convey meaning

## File Operations Best Practices

- Prefer `Path` objects for local filesystem paths
- Atomic file writing for user data, config, state or other where partial output harmful
- Use context managers for file operations
- Handle encoding explicitly (default UTF-8)

## Core Principles

- Pragmatic: avoid over-engineering, premature optimization
- Leverage stdlib first. Use third-party packages sparingly
- Code clarity over clever tricks
- Aim for functional, clean, maintainable, performant code

# Python Development Commands

New or owner-controlled projects → uv. Existing repos → follow project's setup unless asked.

## Package Management with uv

Prefer uv (new projects). Skip `uv pip` unless project uses it. Don't replace other package managers without ask.

```bash
# Initialize new project
uv init

# Add dependencies
uv add package_name
uv add --dev ipykernel pytest ruff basedpyright  # dev dependencies

# Sync dependencies
uv sync

# Show installed packages
uv tree
uv tree --package package_name

# Run commands in virtual environment
uv run python script.py
uv run pytest
```

## Testing with pytest

```bash
# Run all tests
uv run pytest

# Run tests with coverage
uv run pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing

# Run specific test file or function
uv run pytest tests/test_module.py
uv run pytest tests/test_module.py::test_function

# Run tests matching pattern
uv run pytest -k "pattern"

# Run tests with verbose output
uv run pytest -v

# Run tests and stop on first failure
uv run pytest -x
```

## Linting and Formatting with ruff

```bash
# Format code
uv run ruff format .

# Check linting issues
uv run ruff check .

# Fix auto-fixable issues
uv run ruff check --fix .

# Check specific file
uv run ruff check path/to/file.py
```

## Type Checking with basedpyright

```bash
# Type check entire project
uv run basedpyright

# Type check specific file
uv run basedpyright path/to/file.py
```

## Code Quality Checks

```bash
# Run all quality checks (typical CI pipeline)
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run ruff check .
uv run basedpyright
uv run pytest

# Check for common typos
uv run codespell
```

## Profiling and Performance

```bash
# Profile with cProfile
uv run python -m cProfile -s cumtime script.py

# Profile with line_profiler
uv run kernprof -l -v script.py

# Memory profiling
uv run python -m memory_profiler script.py
```

## Common Development Patterns

```bash
# Check outdated packages
uv tree --outdated

# Clean pyc files and caches only when explicitly requested
find . -type d -name "__pycache__" -exec rm -rf {} +
find . -type d -name ".pytest_cache" -exec rm -rf {} +
find . -type d -name ".ruff_cache" -exec rm -rf {} +
find . -type f -name "*.pyc" -delete
```

---
name: log-message-never-repeats-the-host
description: Every pc-switcher log line already carries its host; naming the machine inside the message text is duplication
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Every pc-switcher log record carries the host it happened on (`extra={"host": ...}`, rendered on each line). Do not name the machine inside the message text as well.

**Why:** the host is structural metadata on the line, not part of the sentence. Repeating it makes the message longer without telling the reader anything the line doesn't already show, and it invites splitting one announcement into one-per-host purely to have somewhere to put the name.

**How to apply:** when a message would read "... on pc2", drop that clause and let the line's host carry it. Applies to an action affecting both machines too — announce it once rather than once per host. The exception is text naming a machine that is *not* the line's own host (e.g. "pc1 has X, pc2 has Y" in a comparison, or a remediation command the user runs elsewhere). See [[executor-mutates-marker]] for the other half of what a write must record.

**Why:** the host is structural metadata on the line, not part of the sentence. Repeating it makes the message longer without telling the reader anything the line doesn't already show, and it invites splitting one announcement into one-per-host purely to have somewhere to put the name.

**How to apply:** when a message would read "... on pc2", drop that clause and let the line's host carry it. Applies to an action affecting both machines too — announce it once rather than once per host. The exception is text naming a machine that is *not* the line's own host (e.g. "pc1 has X, pc2 has Y" in a comparison, or a remediation command the user runs elsewhere). See [[executor-mutates-marker]] for the other half of what a write must record.
